title: Define graduated pin-matrix and compatibility notes for new open model intake
creator: Leah Thompson
description:
Problem: Recent intake of community weights shows wide variance in runtime behavior across variants (KV cache sizing, attention kernel compatibility, and sequence-length tail cases). Current onboarding guidance is ambiguous about when a model should be fully pinned versus soft-pinned or allowed to float with compatibility annotations. This ambiguity causes runtime teams to either over-pin (increasing operational burden) or under-pin (causing production regressions).

Goal: Clarify admission requirements and produce a graduated 'pin matrix' and a compatibility-notes template that PMs/engineers/DS can populate during intake. The matrix should map risk signals (kernel incompatibility, quantization sensitivity, memory volatility, eval regression risk) to recommended pin states: Unpinned, Soft-Pin (compat advisory + auto-fallback), and Hard-Pin (runtime-locked).

Scope:
- Define the pin matrix, risk signals, and minimum telemetry checks required for each risk band.
- Create a compatibility-notes template with fields for provenance, alt-variants, known kernel/quantization constraints, mandatory seq_len limits, and KV-cache heuristics.
- Update onboarding checklist and web intake form to require the compatibility-notes and a recommended pin level from the model submitter.
- Provide acceptance criteria and roll-back rules for soft-pin transitions.

Out of scope: automated runtime enforcement (handled by ENG follow-ups) and new kernel implementations.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented pin-matrix artifact exists in Confluence with risk-to-pin mappings and decision examples (low/medium/high risk -> unpinned/soft/hard) and is reviewed by runtime leads.
2) Compatibility-notes template created and added to intake form; intake form rejects submissions missing the template.
3) Onboarding PRD updated with explicit signals and telemetry thresholds (kernel error rate > 0.5% triggers medium risk; memory growth variance > 12% triggers high risk).
4) Three example model intakes (one experimental, one community-stable, one large-variant) have been run through the new flow and annotated notes are attached.
5) Soft-pin policy includes an automatic fallback policy and a rollback checklist; rollout playbook covers how to move from soft-pin -> hard-pin within a 48-hour mitigation window.
6) Cross-functional review completed (Eng, Design, Security) with sign-off recorded in the ticket comments.
notes:
- Telemetry thresholds were derived from a 90-day runtime baseline across popular models.
- Need ENG to expose a 'compatibility_score' metric in the catalog API.
- Product decision: prefer conservative soft-pinning for experimental models to maintain availability while surfacing incompatibilities.
- Risk taxonomy: functional (outputs/regressions), perf (latency/cost), infra (kernel crashes/oom), security (non-deterministic behavior that could cause data leaks).

decisions: Adopt a 3-tier pin taxonomy: Unpinned / Soft-Pin / Hard-Pin.
Soft-Pin requires: compatibility-notes + runtime auto-fallback policy + weekly regression monitoring for first 2 weeks.
Hard-Pin used when kernel_error_rate > 1.5% or memory-volatility > 20% or eval regression severity = high.
Intake submitter must propose a recommended pin; catalog PM will finalize during triage with ENG signal data.
